tips: Add Suica to Apple/Google Wallet while waiting at MSP — land in Tokyo ready to tap.
Fill out Visit Japan Web tonight and screenshot the QRs; airport Wi-Fi can be spotty on arrival.
Hit the Limousine Bus counter at Haneda before the line builds; for 8 people, it's easier than navigating trains with luggage.
Don Quijote recon is smart — wallets closed tonight, but knowing the layout saves time before your flight home.
Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if the group splits, have half do Parco/Nintendo while others queue.
Pre-load your Suica at the konbini if you didn't at MSP — tomorrow's Asakusa-to-Akihabara run requires it.
Senso-ji by 08:30 is the move; by 10:00 the crowds are 5x — set those alarms.
Kamiya Bar near Asakusa is a cheap, historic pre-Skytree stop; the Denki Bran hits harder than you think.
teamLab Planets requires stepping into water — wear easy-off shoes and roll your pants.
Depachika raids are best right before dinner when markdowns start; grab high-end bento boxes for a cheap luxury meal later.
December is peak Mt. Fuji visibility — if the sky is clear, the Enoshima sunset view is a trip highlight.
The Enoden coastal tram gets crowded; try to board at Kamakura Station for a seat.
Ghibli Museum entry is strictly timed; latecomers may not get in — don't let the Shimokitazawa vintage vortex delay you.
Run the Airbnb laundry during dinner so everyone starts the Kyoto leg with a clean kit.
For the Nozomi shinkansen, seats E and D offer the best Fuji view around minute 40 out of Tokyo.
Pontocho Alley dinner for 8 is a huge win; don't be late or the reservation may be given away.
Fushimi Inari at 06:45 is cold but magical — hand warmers from a konbini are mandatory.
Funaoka Onsen's electric bath is an experience, but don't overstay; 3 seconds is enough for first-timers.
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove by 07:15 beats the buses; if you want photos without strangers, walk fast.
Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter — skip the climb and spend that time at Kasuga Taisha instead.
Pre-order your KFC Christmas Bucket NOW if you haven't — they sell out weeks in advance for the 24th.
Nintendo Museum lottery tickets are locked, but Uji's Byodo-in and matcha scene is a worthy backup if anyone missed out.
USJ Express Passes are essential for Super Nintendo World on a holiday; rope-drop the gates 45 min early.
If the group splits, the Osaka Aquarium is a world-class alternative that avoids the USJ crowds entirely.
This is the longest day of the trip; the Peace Museum is emotionally heavy — it's okay to take a quiet walk in Shukkei-en after.
Golden hour at Miyajima is early in winter; catch the 16:45 ferry back to maximize the torii silhouette shots.
Midosuji Illumination is 4km of lights; start at Umeda and walk south so you end up near Namba for dinner.
551 Horai butaman sell out nightly — grab a 4-pack at Namba station before the crab feast for tomorrow's breakfast.
Himeji Castle has a lot of steep stairs; wear good shoes and ditch heavy bags in the coin lockers at the station.
Do a tax-free receipt check tonight — make sure passports are printed on receipts and items are accessible for customs.
For the shinkansen back, grab seats on the LEFT (A/E) for one last Mt. Fuji view if the sky is clear.
Zero out your Suica cards at the Haneda kiosks or spend the balance on final boss gachapon before security.

globalTips: The USD/JPY rate is highly favorable at ~161.5 JPY to 1 USD — use credit cards with no foreign transaction fees for large purchases to maximize the rate, but carry cash for smaller shops and ramen counters.
For a group of 8, always send a scout to hold the line at restaurants while the rest of the group arrives — popular spots like Ichiran or Tsukiji will have waits that multiply with a large party.
Winter days in Japan are short (sunset around 16:30-17:00); plan all outdoor sightseeing and illumination walks for the early afternoon to dusk window to avoid missing key sights in the dark.
